title: AddTenantCostRollup migration fails on TimescaleDB ≥2.18 — RLS after columnstore enable is rejected; blocks every deploy
evidence: log: aqua-db-migrate ... migration: AddTenantCostRollup1805000000000, error: operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled
rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 reframes `timescaledb.compress` as columnstore mode on the hypertable; once columnstore is on, the engine rejects subsequent vanilla `ALTER TABLE ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. Migrations that touch hypertable RLS must run RLS *before* the compression configuration, not after.
notes: Symptom: db-migrate container exits with `Migration failed ... operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled` BEFORE any service container starts; entire deploy chain blocks at this single migration. Architectural fix (T1, reorder operations to honour columnstore lock-out): up() now runs CREATE TABLE → CREATE INDEX → RLS (ENABLE/FORCE/CREATE POLICY) → create_hypertable → SET (timescaledb.compress, ...) → add_compression_policy → add_retention_policy. down() reordered to remove TimescaleDB policies first, then DROP TABLE CASCADE — avoids the columnstore-vs-ALTER restriction entirely (no intermediate ALTER TABLE / DROP POLICY needed; CASCADE tears down policies, RLS state, indexes, hypertable metadata, columnstore chunks in one shot). Sensor-service migration (sensor-service/src/database/migrations/1735900000000-CreateSensorMetrics.ts) audited and is unaffected — it has compression but no RLS, so no ordering conflict.

title: AddTenantCostRollup migration — TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces RLS ⊥ columnstore mutual exclusion; reorder alone insufficient
evidence: log: error: "columnstore cannot be used on table with row security"
rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces a HARD MUTUAL EXCLUSION between RLS and columnstore on the same hypertable. The RLS-first reorder under INFRA-CRITICAL-006 traded `operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled` (compression-then-RLS) for `columnstore cannot be used on table with row security` (RLS-then-compression). Engine refuses both sequences — order does not unlock either side.
notes:
Architectural fork (must pick ONE):
  (A) keep columnstore, drop RLS — moves tenant isolation enforcement entirely to the service layer.
  (B) keep RLS, drop columnstore — preserves DB-level defense-in-depth, loses ~50% storage savings on cold buckets.

Decision: (B). User-confirmed (response: 'b'). Rationale:
- Multi-tenant SaaS — tenant isolation is the load-bearing invariant; RLS is the DB-level guard.
- Table scale at documented retention: ~29k rows/day × 90 days = ~2.6M rows total; PostgreSQL handles this trivially.
- Compression savings (~1-2 GB/year) are immaterial vs the integrity guarantee.
- Future cold-storage compression can be reintroduced via a continuous aggregate (no RLS on the aggregate, RLS-equivalent filter pushed into the materialized query) when the dataset grows enough to justify it.

Fix landed:
- Removed `ALTER TABLE … SET (timescaledb.compress, …)` block.
- Removed `add_compression_policy(…, INTERVAL '14 days', …)` call.
- Kept `create_hypertable` (for chunking) + `add_retention_policy(…, INTERVAL '90 days', …)` (for time-based pruning).
- Kept full RLS (ENABLE + FORCE + tenant_scope policy + observability_service_admin bypass).
- Down(): removed `remove_compression_policy` call (nothing to remove).
- Inline load-bearing comment documents the constraint, the architectural fork, and the chosen branch with rationale, so any future engineer attempting to add columnstore back will see the trade-off.

title: Boot signal `migration_runner_applied` never fires after db-migrate centralization — pattern only matched cold-start hot path
evidence: Deploy log run 24636862240 (boot signal assertion: 23 signal(s) pending across 12 services for 12+ rounds, all healthy)
rule_violated: WS7 / ADR-016 Phase F deploy gate: every service in required-signals.yaml MUST emit each declared signal within its window. After db-migrate centralization, every service's migration runner sees 0 pending migrations on warm start and logs `No pending migrations on "<schema>"` — that text does NOT contain the substring `migration(s)` (with parens), so the signal never matches and the deploy gate rejects every deploy even though all containers are healthy and migrations have been applied centrally.
notes:
Architectural fix (T1, single canonical signal source):

1. MigrationRunnerService.onApplicationBootstrap() now emits a canonical end-of-run log line — `Migration runner complete for schema "<sourceSchema>": tenants=<N>` — at the success exit. Fires unconditionally on both cold-start (>0 pending applied) and warm-start (0 pending) paths. Failure paths (security throw, runner exception) intentionally do NOT emit it, so the contract still proves the runner reached the success exit (no false positive).
2. required-signals.yaml signal_library.migration_runner_applied pattern updated from `"migration(s)"` (substring of "Applied N migration(s): …") to `"Migration runner complete"` (substring of the new canonical line).
3. The pre-existing per-schema logs (`Applied N migration(s) on "X"` and `No pending migrations on "X"`) are unchanged — they still document per-schema progress; they're just no longer the contract surface for the deploy gate.
4. Refactored the orphan `if (!tenantAware) return;` early-return into a single tenantAware branch so the canonical complete log lands once per runner invocation regardless of fan-out shape.

Why not change the signal pattern alone: a looser substring like `"migration"` would match `migration failed`, `running migration`, etc. — any noise word that happens to mention migrations would falsely satisfy the contract. The canonical-log approach pins the signal to a single emission point in the code, which is the discipline required by required-signals.yaml's signalSource convention.

title: GraphQL enum input coercion drops value-mapping → uppercase 'MEMBER' written to DB violates chk_member_role
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240275 log: new row for relation channel_members violates check constraint chk_member_role; failing row contains ... MEMBER, all, ...
rule_violated: TypeScript enum ChannelMemberRole has key MEMBER mapped to value 'member'. registerEnumType(ChannelMemberRole, { name: 'ChannelMemberRole' }) without explicit valuesMap leaks the enum NAME ('MEMBER') through to resolver param → command → handler → SQL. CHECK constraint allows lowercase only ('owner','admin','member'). Per OWASP input-boundary discipline, enum coercion must be the canonical normalization point.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, canonical input boundary normalization): replace bare registerEnumType with explicit valuesMap so GraphQL→TypeScript coercion writes the TypeScript enum VALUE, not the NAME. If valuesMap alone insufficient (NestJS GraphQL edge case for value-mapped string enums), add @Transform on AddChannelMemberInput DTO that maps GraphQL name to enum value. Apply same pattern to NotificationPreference. Add apps/messaging-service/src/channel/__tests__/role-enum-coercion.spec.ts as contract test.

title: Runtime dataSource.synchronize() in SourceSchemaBootstrapService creates wrong-shape columns + crashes on partitioned-table FK
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240275 deploy log: SourceSchemaBootstrapService Failed to bootstrap source schema ... there is no unique constraint matching given keys for referenced table messages
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md forbids dataSource.synchronize() in runtime: migrations are SSoT. NestJS onModuleInit fires BEFORE onApplicationBootstrap, so SourceSchemaBootstrapService runs synchronize before MessagingMigrationRunnerService. TypeORM 0.3.x cannot generate composite FK to partitioned messages(id, createdAt). Same synchronize call also creates columns with wrong nullability — silently corrupts every fresh DB.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, eliminate the contaminant): remove both synchronize() calls; move lifecycle hook from onModuleInit to onApplicationBootstrap with provider ordering after MessagingMigrationRunnerService; replace empty-schema branch with hard-fail message instructing operator to run db-migrate. Add tests/invariants/no-runtime-synchronize.spec.ts that greps the entire repo and asserts zero synchronize() callsites outside test setup files.

title: message_attachments.is_deleted partial index pending — needs CONCURRENTLY migration
rule_violated: Entity declares @Index() on is_deleted as a performance optimization for non-deleted-attachment lookups. The drift remediation migration could not include CREATE INDEX because R3 (migration-sql-lint) requires CONCURRENTLY for indexes on populated tables, and CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transactional migration.
notes: Follow-up: write a sibling migration with transactional=false that runs `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_attachments_is_deleted ON message_attachments (is_deleted) WHERE is_deleted = false`. Tenant-aware fan-out applies (one CONCURRENT index per source + per tenant schema). Performance-only optimization; not a correctness invariant; drift validator does NOT flag missing indexes so this does not re-open the deploy gate.

title: Illegal `value:` field in registerEnumType valuesMap blocks tsc — 12/12 messaging E2E + CI Affected backend build fail
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24638245324 (E2E messaging) job 72037454378 — 12/12 suites failed to compile, 0 tests run
GitHub Actions run 24638245327 (CI Affected) job 72037594216 — backend build failed with 12 TS2353 errors
rule_violated: NestJS EnumMetadataValuesMapOptions only accepts description? + deprecationReason?. The `value` field does not exist in the type signature. tsc --strict rejects unknown properties in mapped type literals. NestJS controls enum value coercion via the enum's own Object.entries(enum) — valuesMap is metadata-only.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, delete the dead-and-illegal field): remove the `, value: <Enum>.<KEY>` from each of the 6 valuesMap entries. Keep description-only. The actual GraphQL-name → TS-value boundary normalization lives in channel.resolver.ts:227 via `(ChannelMemberRole as Record<string, ChannelMemberRole>)[role] ?? role`. That's the canonical T1 coercion fix; the valuesMap was a misunderstood secondary attempt. No functional regression — runtime behaviour was already correct via the resolver normalization, the illegal field just blocked compilation.

evidence: GitHub Actions run 24653206569 deploy job 72081278019: 'Container aqua-postgres Error dependency postgres failed to start; container is unhealthy'
docker-compose.droplet.yml:162 image timescale/timescaledb-ha:pg16 (HA edition, Ubuntu base, postgres uid=1000)
Earlier image timescale/timescaledb:2.25.1-pg16 (Alpine base, postgres uid=999)
rule_violated: Image-family-coupled hardcoding violates the 'works with any postgres image' contract that container entrypoints should honor. The pgvector image swap (commit b11bac15) silently broke production cert ownership because the entrypoint script assumed Alpine uid conventions.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, image-agnostic uid resolution): replace hardcoded `chown 999:999` with `chown $(id -u postgres):$(id -g postgres)`. Falls back to 999 only if the user doesn't exist. Works on Alpine (uid 999), Debian/Ubuntu (uid 1000), and any future image with a `postgres` user. The certs now get the correct ownership regardless of which postgres image the compose file references. Production deploy chain unblocked once this lands and the droplet pulls the updated entrypoint script.

title: MODULE_SCHEMAS lists orphan tables (supplier_sites, site_contacts) — SourceSchemaBootstrapService crashes farm-service
evidence: apps/farm-service/src/supplier/entities/supplier-site.entity.ts:7-10 ('Orphan entity - not registered in any module forFeature')
Live droplet logs: 'Source schema farm is missing 2/69 declared tables: supplier_sites, site_contacts'
rule_violated: Per ADR-011, MODULE_SCHEMAS lists ACTIVE tables only. Orphan @Entity() declarations are entity-side tech debt, not schema ownership claims. Listing them crashed SourceSchemaBootstrapService after INFRA-CRITICAL-009 made missing-table verification hard-fail.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, MODULE_SCHEMAS reflects active tables only): remove supplier_sites + site_contacts from farm MODULE_SCHEMAS.tables. Inline comment documents the orphan status. When architectural decision to USE these entities is taken, write migration AND re-add to MODULE_SCHEMAS in SAME commit.

title: HA postgres image default PGDATA path differs from legacy image — initdb fails on existing volume
evidence: Live droplet log: 'initdb: error: directory /home/postgres/pgdata/data exists but is not empty'
rule_violated: Image-family-specific PGDATA defaults break compose volume reuse. The pgvector image swap (b11bac15) silently changed the postgres data directory expectation; the existing volume mount points at the legacy path; HA image's initdb tries to bootstrap a different (image-baked, mostly-empty) directory and fails because it's not empty.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, explicit PGDATA pin across all compose files): set PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data env var explicitly in docker-compose.{droplet,prod,dev,infra,base}.yml so the HA image uses the same data path as the legacy image. Single source of truth across every environment. Combined with INFRA-CRITICAL-017 (dynamic uid resolution) + the one-shot volume chown (70 → 1000) on the droplet, postgres now boots cleanly from existing data using the new HA image.

title: Messaging E2E race: SourceSchemaBootstrapService.onApplicationBootstrap fires BEFORE MessagingMigrationRunnerService
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24655383286 messaging E2E job 72087509759: 'Source schema messaging is empty AFTER application bootstrap... Refusing to fall back to runtime synchronize() per INFRA-CRITICAL-009'
12/12 test suites failed at bootstrap stage; 0 tests ran
rule_violated: Both SourceSchemaBootstrapService and MessagingMigrationRunnerService register onApplicationBootstrap. NestJS calls them in declaration order; SourceSchemaBootstrapService fires FIRST and finds an empty source schema (migrations haven't run yet). My INFRA-CRITICAL-009 hard-fail then kills the bootstrap. Production is unaffected (aqua-db-migrate runs before service container starts, per compose dependency chain) but E2E tests boot the AppModule directly and have no such pre-stage.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, env-aware migration timing): add migrationsRunFromEnv to messaging-service's createServiceTypeOrmConfig call. Test (DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_RUN=true) → TypeORM runs migrations at DataSource init, BEFORE any NestJS lifecycle hook fires → SourceBootstrap finds tables → no false-fail. Production (DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_RUN=false) → unchanged, aqua-db-migrate runs first via compose. The MessagingMigrationRunnerService becomes a verify-only no-op in both paths but stays as defense-in-depth.

title: Cross-service entity contamination via @aquaculture/backend-common main barrel — every service auto-loads AuditLogEntity/UserConsent/GdprDataRequest/FindingEntity, surfacing as ~30 cross-schema drift violations per service
evidence: Live droplet drift output 2026-04-20: farm-service=89 violations, admin-api=132, billing=33, sensor=35, alert=30, auth=40, hr=24, notification=25, config=25, observability=3, hydroponics=1 — 30+ are cross-schema entity contamination
libs/backend-common/src/index.ts had `export * from './audit'` + `export * from './finding-registry'` triggering @Entity decorator side-effects on every consumer
libs/backend-common/src/security/index.ts had `export * from './gdpr'` triggering UserConsent + GdprDataRequest decorators

libs/backend-common/src/guards/tenant.guard.ts imported AuditLogService directly, chaining through audit-log.entity.ts → @Entity decorator runs in every service that uses TenantGuard (which is every service)
rule_violated: ADR-011 schema ownership: each entity belongs to exactly one service's schema. The transitive import-time @Entity decorator side-effect via the shared backend-common barrel made every service co-own foreign entities, breaking the SchemaDriftValidator's per-service ownership contract.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, dependency-inversion + barrel surgery): (1) New audit-log.tokens.ts file owns AUDIT_LOG_SERVICE Symbol token + IAuditLogService interface + AuditSeverity enum — NO @Entity import. (2) tenant.guard.ts depends on token+interface (not concrete AuditLogService class). (3) audit-log.module.ts provides AUDIT_LOG_SERVICE token alongside concrete class so existing concrete-class consumers stay green. (4) backend-common/src/index.ts no longer re-exports `./audit` or `./finding-registry`; security/index.ts no longer re-exports `./gdpr` — these are deep-import only via tsconfig path aliases @aquaculture/backend-common/{audit,gdpr,finding-registry}. (5) 10 consumer files mechanically rewritten to use the deep paths. (6) Invariant test tests/invariants/no-shared-entity-decorators-via-main-barrel.spec.ts locks the contract.

title: DEFECT-2: ~213 @Entity() decorators across 11 services declared no schema option, defaulting to 'public' and tripping the SchemaDriftValidator on every cold start
evidence: Live droplet drift output 2026-04-20: farm=89 violations, admin-api=132, billing=33, sensor=35, alert=30, auth=40, hr=24, notification=25, config=25, observability=3, hydroponics=1 — ~400 of these reduce to the missing schema option
Sample violation per service: '[farms] entity declares schema=public but table lives in farm', '[invoices] entity declares schema=public but table lives in billing', etc.
ADR-011 + CLAUDE.md Inviolable rule #2: Every @Entity() includes the schema: option. The mechanical convention had drifted across ~213 entity files.
rule_violated: ADR-011 schema ownership: every @Entity() must declare its schema explicitly so the SchemaDriftValidator can verify entity↔table alignment without false positives from the TypeORM 'schema=public' default.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, mechanical sweep + invariant): added { schema: '<svc>' } to 213 @Entity decorator calls across 185 files in 11 services (admin-api, auth, billing, config, event-store, farm, alert-engine, ai, hydroponics, sensor, plus a few in observability). Codemod handled three @Entity argument shapes: (1) @Entity('table') → adds 2nd arg, (2) @Entity('table', { ...opts }) → merges schema into opts, (3) @Entity({ name: 'table', ...opts }) → merges schema into opts. New invariant tests/invariants/entity-schema-declaration.spec.ts walks every apps/*/src/**/*.entity.ts and asserts every non-empty @Entity call carries a schema: option — locks the contract.

title: Phase D: env-aware migrationsRun was missing from 8 services that use MigrationRunnerService — every E2E test of those services would crash on SourceSchemaBootstrapService just like INFRA-CRITICAL-020 messaging E2E did
evidence: INFRA-CRITICAL-020 (commit 074c7807) added migrationsRunFromEnv to messaging-service to unblock E2E. The same race exists for every other service that uses MigrationRunnerService — when an E2E harness boots the AppModule against a fresh DB, SourceSchemaBootstrapService.onApplicationBootstrap fires before any migration runner could populate the schema, hard-failing per INFRA-CRITICAL-009.

8 services lacked migrationsRunFromEnv: farm, hr, alert-engine, billing, notification, config, hydroponics, ai. Discovered via `grep -L migrationsRunFromEnv apps/*-service/src/app.module.ts apps/alert-engine/src/app.module.ts`

messaging-service had it (074c7807); sensor-service had it (different default); admin-api/event-store had it (legacy 'true' default); auth uses `migrationsRun: true`; observability has `migrations: []`
rule_violated: Service migration-timing contract (INFRA-CRITICAL-020): every service that owns a source schema AND uses MigrationRunnerService must opt into the env-aware TypeORM runner so test harnesses can apply migrations before NestJS lifecycle hooks fire.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, mechanical sweep): added the env-aware migrationsRunFromEnv block to 8 services' createServiceTypeOrmConfig calls. Default 'false' = production-safe (aqua-db-migrate runs first in prod). E2E harnesses set DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_RUN=true to enable TypeORM's built-in runner at DataSource init. New invariant tests/invariants/all-services-env-aware-migrations.spec.ts asserts every service has the contract (or one of three documented alternatives: legacy 'true' default for admin-api/event-store, static migrationsRun:true for auth, migrations:[] for observability).
